title: Integer Division
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how // divides and keeps only the whole number part.
learn: See that // drops the decimal part
Compare / and // on the same numbers
idea: The operator // is integer division, also called floor division. It divides and keeps only the whole part, so 7 // 2 is 3 and not 3.5. Use / when you want the decimal and // when you only care about whole pieces, like how many full teams you can make.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change players = 23 to players = 25 and press Run. The last line should say Full teams: 5.

practice.text: Use // to find how many full weeks are in 30 days. Print the answer.
practice.hint: One week is 7 days. Integer division // drops the leftover days, so you only get whole weeks.
practice.starterTip: Try weeks = days // 7 on the blank line (30 // 7 is 4).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if weeks is 4 (30 // 7) and printed. Must use //.

practice.text: Print both 19 / 5 and 19 // 5 on separate lines so you can compare them.
practice.hint: You need two print() lines. One uses / for the decimal answer and the other uses // for the whole number only.
practice.starterTip: First line print(19 / 5), second line print(19 // 5). Run and compare 3.8 vs 3.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if one print shows 3.8 (or similar float) and one shows 3 using //.

quiz.question: What is 9 // 2?
quiz.correct: Right, // keeps only the whole part, so 9 // 2 is 4.
quiz.wrong: Integer division drops the .5, so 9 // 2 is 4.

quiz.question: Which operator drops the decimal part after dividing?
quiz.wrong: / keeps the decimals and // keeps only the whole number.

quiz.question: You have 14 muffins and boxes of 5. How many full boxes with //?
quiz.wrong: 14 divided by 5 is 2 with some left over, and // gives you the 2.
